answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It survives because finality only counts for established attestators, so a fresh cluster cannot push transactions until it proves honesty across many epochs.
